title: A frame-layout ceiling for #200's bit word: coarse < 6.964e-4 under the banked ledger, so κ < 6.959e-4 on #205–#207's word (no new κ)
body:
Adds `research/bit-frame-ceiling-200/` and one workflow; **no existing file changes and no new κ.** This carries DaysSky's #192 frame-floor method from #168's complex word to the physical bit word that #200, #205, #206 and #207 share. #200 is not on main, so the package carries the eight files of #200 it reads (frozen physical bit word, frames, partner chronology, graph, profile, sinks, certificate and the retained PR168-v4 exact integer checker) as a pinned archive `baseline-pr200.tar.gz` (1.4 MB), every sha256 pinned in `SOURCE.json` to commit `a1175449`; reviewers can confirm with `git show a1175449:<path> | sha256sum` or rebuild the archive byte for byte with `git archive --format=tar a1175449 <paths> | gzip -n -9`.

## Result

For every admissible choice of operation frames on this word (DAG, operations, sources, gauges, 1,760 reuse pairs, partner chronology and 34 sinks fixed):

| Ledger | Floor on C | Coarse saving ceiling | κ ceiling | Standing |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| #200's own (entrance tails charged) | 2,804,210 | **6.904e-4** | 6.900e-4 | #200's 6.7777e-4 is 98.2% of it |
| completed entrance banks (#205/#206/#207) | 2,780,144 | **6.964e-4** | **6.959e-4** | #207's bit coarse 6.8366e-4 is 98.2% of it |
| without coupling the two registers of an operation | | 7.056e-4 / 7.118e-4 | | |

Consequences:

- Frame refinement on this word is worth at most **+1.8%** more on the bit side, under either ledger. #207's 302 coordinated changes are already inside this margin.
- The ceiling 6.964e-4 lies **below** the complex supplier those PRs use (#202's source-assisted word, 7.009e-4, itself at #192's ceiling for its frames). So on this bit word the complex branch can never bind, and every κ assembled from it stays below 6.959e-4 whatever the bit frames. Going further needs a different bit word (circuit, reuse, gauges or sinks), a bank construction that removes other children than the entrance tails, or a different design (#201 bounds the design at 2.5592e-3).

## Argument

`D = 2v − 3ℓ = 1,936`, `C = Σ n_r·r·ln(m/r)`, `m = 72`.

1. Every certified coarse saving satisfies `a < D/C` (#192 Lemma 1; on #200 the gap is 0.088%).
2. Every retained assembly accepts κ only below `a/(1+a)` of the binding supplier (#183), the atom wrapper and the finite stopped-leaf bootstrap of #185/#197/#207 stay below the coarse saving they start from.
3. Splitting a frame climb into more steps only costs more (`r·ln(m/r)` is subadditive).
4. No frame layout of the word pushes `C` below a floor: joint bounds propagated through both registers of every operation, an exact per-register dynamic programme over frame dimensions, and Lagrangian coupling of the two registers (1,200 integer subgradient rounds; each round is itself a valid floor).

The terminal record of #200's `bit/terminal.py` substitutes exactly one child of width 3 (the sink's root-to-full step, present in every layout) and one target child of width 21 per sink and stage and keeps the sink's other steps charged on the pivot; the script checks this against the certificate's `child_delta` and the pre/post target histograms, so the floor of the terminal ledger is the pre-sink floor minus that fixed cost. The banked ledger drops only the entrance tails `3·dim σ`, which is the only child change the completed-bank constructions make; their bank proofs are not re-verified here and the ceiling does not depend on them.

[PROOF.md](https://github.com/chafreaky/integer-mult-bounds/blob/research/bit-frame-ceiling-200/research/bit-frame-ceiling-200/PROOF.md) has the statements and proofs.

## Verify

    python3 research/bit-frame-ceiling-200/ceiling.py --check     # stdlib only, about 2.5 minutes; -O is refused

The script rebuilds the pinned #200 files after checking the archive and every file hash, prepares the retained exact integer checker's geometry, and checks itself: #200's layout lies inside every derived frame bound; its slot chains reproduce #200's certified pre-sink ledger child for child (W 20,668; rank 1,486,160) and the −102/−102 terminal substitution; every per-slot floor and every Lagrangian round lies below #200's actual cost. All bounds use exact integers with rounded-down rational logarithms, so the printed ceilings are upper bounds. `--tree PATH` runs on a #200 checkout; `--overrides FILE` prices another layout of the same word: on #207's `frames/opframe-bases.json` it confirms the 302-frame layout lies inside every bound and above the floor, with banked `D/C = 6.8427e-4` (98.3% of the ceiling).

Run before opening: `--check` passes from the archive alone and on a #200 checkout (Python 3.14, macOS), with and without #207's overrides. The new workflow runs `--check` on Python 3.11 and 3.14.

## Scope and limits

- One word only: constructions that change the DAG, pairs, gauges, sinks or the bank construction are not bounded.
- Elementary proofs, not machine-checked beyond the script's exact arithmetic and self-tests; no one else has reviewed them.
